start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the workflow for <what I want done>, then start it." Your AI runs the wf command on this computer: wf find WORDS, then wf start WORKFLOW_ID with the input.
no_lists_because: wf reads the workflow definitions this computer keeps and the store a run names; it writes run folders on this computer. No list of yours is read or written by the host itself.
instructions: 1. Install it once from the Workshop: tools/workflows/build-wf.sh builds the package from origin/main into the bin folder wf runs from.
2. wf find WORDS lists the workflows that fit the words; wf kinds WORDS lists the kinds to search by.
3. wf start WORKFLOW_ID - reads the input from standard input; wf answer RUN STEP - answers a waiting step; wf show RUN shows where a run is.

worked_examples.title: Start a found workflow
worked_examples.ask: Find the workflow for sending a tour to a student, then start it for the student named in my message
worked_examples.given: The installed Workshop has the workflow definition workflow:send-a-tour; the input names the student.
worked_examples.hands_back: wf start prints the run folder and its status: "completed" when every step is answered, or "paused" with what each waiting step asks.
